title: DuckStation repurposes the DualSense mute LED as an analog-mode indicator
summary: An opt-in output link mirrors the emulated controller's analog state on hardware users can actually see, restoring feedback that modern PlayStation pads otherwise lack.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from DuckStation pull request #3574: Use DualSense Mic Mute LED for Analog Mode

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3574: Use DualSense Mic Mute LED for Analog Mode

blocks.text: Modern controllers lost the LED that explained PlayStation analog state

Original Dual Analog and DualShock controllers gave players a visible indication when analog mode was enabled. DualSense and DualSense Edge have richer output hardware but no equivalent light dedicated to the old PlayStation mode. Games and controller hotkeys can still change that emulated state, leaving a user with no physical confirmation unless the emulator UI is visible.
The microphone-mute LED becomes an optional output target

Pull request #3574 adds a preference that maps analog-mode status to the DualSense microphone-mute LED. The controller continues to report buttons and axes normally; only the chosen output light is repurposed. Making the behavior optional avoids claiming ownership of an LED some users rely on for its native microphone meaning, while still offering a close visual analogue to the original pad indicator.
Analog state is shared across several emulated controller classes

The change touches Analog Controller, Analog Joystick, Jogcon, NeGcon, and NeGcon Rumble paths together with input types and the input manager. That breadth matters because the LED should reflect the emulated device's mode, not merely whether a DualShock profile screen is open. Fullscreen and Qt settings expose the same choice so the output does not depend on which frontend configured the controller.
Testing must verify state transitions and native mute behavior

Connect DualSense and DualSense Edge devices separately, toggle analog mode through every supported hotkey or game command, and confirm LED state follows without lag or inversion. Repeat with each affected emulated controller class and after unplug, reconnect, pause, and state load. With the option disabled, DuckStation must stop driving the light so normal microphone feedback remains available. Other controller models should ignore the setting without errors or phantom output devices.
The LED mapping restores hardware feedback only when requested; it does not redefine the DualSense mute light for every user.
